value.body: Prosecutors conduct criminal cases on behalf of the State. Assistant Public Prosecutors (APPs) appear in magistrates' courts; Public Prosecutors and Additional Public Prosecutors appear in sessions courts. APP posts are filled by state governments, usually through the state Public Service Commission, under Section 19 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), 2023.

items.label: APP appointment
items.value: By the state government, for each district

items.label: Public Prosecutor eligibility
items.value: At least 7 years as an advocate
items.note: BNSS 2023, Section 18(7); prosecuting service can count

items.label: APP practice requirement
items.note: From none to several years at the Bar

value.title: How you get in
value.body: An LLB and enrolment with a State Bar Council; many states also ask for a minimum period of practice. Apply when the state PSC or prosecution department notifies APP posts. Selection is usually a written exam on criminal law and procedure, often followed by a main exam and interview, within the state's age limits.

value.title: At a glance
items: Notifications are irregular and state-specific; your state's service rules set the details.
The work is criminal-law heavy — BNS, BNSS and BSA, which replaced the IPC, CrPC and Evidence Act in July 2024.
Central prosecutors, such as those for the CBI, are recruited separately.
